solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Aha! Malay a basis for my domain tongue

definitions.note: .my is the internet domain of Malaysia, so its tongue is the national language

indicators.note: read loosely as 'used for making', so the letters before it are to be reworked into a new phrase

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims on finding that Malay underpins the language of their own territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen letters of AHA MALAY A BASIS rearrange to give the answer; 'my' is the country-code web domain, not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the official name of the national language of Malaysia, the country whose web suffix is .my.

clue.text: Display health food

definitions.meaning: to wave something about for show
a bowl of bran, read as a two-word phrase, is a wholesome serving

explanation.surface: A shop window shows off wholesome produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving a sword about is a showy display; split in two the word is a cereal-husk serving.

clue.text: Look among two farm animals for 3-D image

indicators.note: one piece sits among the letters of the other, so it goes inside

parts.note: a hog (pig) and a ram (male sheep)
LO is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: An instruction to search between a pig and a sheep for a three-dimensional picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser-made picture that appears to have depth is a three-dimensional image.

clue.text: Rambler way in front and more off-beat

indicators.note: the way's abbreviation goes before the walker, at the front of the word

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
a ranger is one who roams or rambles

explanation.surface: A hiker striding well ahead and behaving more eccentrically.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word for odd or unusual, matching the comparative 'more off-beat'.

clue.text: See 1
Give guarantee when certain

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Promise only when you are confident.
explanation.definitionFit: To promise someone firmly is to give them a guarantee.

clue.text: Notice a dry object

parts.note: TT means teetotal, i.e. dry
an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: Observe an arid thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed or pay attention to something is to notice it.

clue.text: The way to bemuse setter

indicators.note: to bemuse is to confuse, so the letters of setter are muddled

explanation.surface: How to baffle the crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the compiler but is just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A road in a town is a way, as in many street names.

clue.text: Zola's charge

parts.note: Emile Zola's famous open letter in the Dreyfus affair bore a French title meaning 'I charge', which supplies the verb

explanation.surface: The allegation made by the French novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone with wrongdoing is to blame them formally; Zola's letter title used the French form.

clue.text: Every river is an attraction

parts.note: all means every
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Each river has its appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm or enticing quality is a synonym for attraction.

clue.text: Mysterious drugs to upset Morecambe

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so ES is drugs

indicators.note: in a down clue sense, upset turns the little word over, back to front

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a British comedian

explanation.surface: Puzzling narcotics that disturb a comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Morecambe was half of a famous British comedy double act; 'upset' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obscure, understood only by a few, is mysterious.

clue.text: Enjoyed touching tail of charming mermaid?

parts.note: dug is slang for liked or enjoyed
on means touching or against

indicators.note: the tail is the final letter of the word charming

explanation.surface: Delighting in contact with the end of an enchanting sea maiden.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: sailors' sightings of this animal may have started mermaid legends.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea cow is popularly thought to have inspired sailors' tales of mermaids.

clue.text: SS in pursuit of George and Charlotte

indicators.note: following behind, so the two letters come after the royal title

parts.note: Prince George, son of the Prince of Wales

explanation.surface: A steamship chasing two royal children.
explanation.walkthrough: George and Charlotte are children of Prince William.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte, sister of George, is a royal daughter with that title.

clue.text: Threads for crashing out

parts.note: threads is slang for clothes, and crashing out is going to sleep

explanation.surface: Wire or yarn for crashing out of a system.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is clothing worn for sleeping, or collapsing into bed.

clue.text: No contest for free run

definitions.meaning: in a tournament, passing to the next round without playing
in cricket, a run scored without the batter hitting the ball

explanation.surface: A walkover granted for an unopposed jog.
explanation.definitionFit: In knockouts it is an unplayed passage onward; in cricket it is an extra run conceded by the fielding side.

clue.text: Small bed for Buffy, perhaps

parts.note: a bed is a layer, as of rock

explanation.surface: A little cot for a girl called Buffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffy is the vampire killer of the TV series 'Buffy the Vampire ...', an example of a killer.

clue.text: Spirit captured back live from Uranus

indicators.note: the captured letters are read backwards
the letters are held captive within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A ghost recorded in a broadcast from a distant planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' takes MUR from 'froM URanus'; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A distilled liquor made from sugar cane is a spirit.

clue.text: No.1 crackpot

parts.note: the one printed word is read as an instruction, crack pot: break up the three letters of pot and rearrange them; that the result shows reversed inside the word is a coincidence of this shuffle, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: The chief eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackpot' reads as one word, but splits as 'crack' (break up) and 'pot', whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading or first-ranked one is said to be number one, the head of the list.

clue.text: Manage a donkey almost in a frenzy

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: the word is nearly complete, missing its last letter

parts.note: moke is slang for a donkey

explanation.surface: Handling a nearly-complete ass in a state of panic.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is British slang for a donkey; 'almost' cuts it to MOK.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave wildly and uncontrollably is to act in a frenzy.

clue.text: GPS, a monk reorientated for some villages

indicators.note: turned round to face a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A satnav device and a monk redirected towards rural settlements.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Malay settlements or hamlets, an example of villages.

clue.text: Present time singer

parts.note: present time is Christmas, gift-giving time, when people sing seasonal songs door to door

explanation.surface: A vocalist of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present time' looks like 'nowadays' but means the season of gifts.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasonal singer performs festive songs at Christmas, the time of presents.

clue.text: A swimmer a newspaper turned to jelly

parts.note: a gar is a fish

indicators.note: turned round, so the word is reversed

parts.note: rag is slang for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A fish and a tabloid that became gelatinous.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatinous substance from seaweed used to set foods is a jelly.

clue.text: Accident involving a knife

indicators.note: the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: prang is British slang for a crash or accident

explanation.surface: A mishap with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A Malay machete or large chopping blade is a kind of knife.

clue.text: No rot in arboretum cultivating tropical hard wood

indicators.note: means the letters of rot are absent from the larger word
tending the soil, working over, so the letters left are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rot-free tree garden growing exotic timber.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R, O, T from ARBORETUM and rearrange the rest (ABEUMR).
explanation.definitionFit: A Southeast Asian timber tree prized for durable flooring is a tropical hardwood.

clue.text: Extremist to booze a lot of bottles

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it in, so the words contain the answer

explanation.surface: A fanatic downing many bottles of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like containers of drink but means 'contains'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanatic devoted zealously to a cause is an extremist.

clue.text: One-dimensional king accepting only the popular

indicators.note: taking another in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's king
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A shallow monarch who admits only fashionable people.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged along a line, so having length alone, is one-dimensional.

clue.text: Many hours for Doris

definitions.meaning: twenty-four hours is a full span
Doris ... was an American actress and singer

explanation.surface: Long hours put in for a woman named Doris.
explanation.definitionFit: A span of twenty-four hours is many hours; it is also the surname of the singer Doris.

clue.text: Fruit for desperate character who embraced spoonbender

indicators.note: held round, so one name goes inside the other

parts.note: Desperate Dan, a cowboy in the British comic The Dandy
Uri Geller, famous for bending spoons

explanation.surface: Produce for a frantic person who hugged a spoon-bending showman.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a British comic-strip strongman; Uri Geller is a showman known for bending cutlery.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiky Southeast Asian fruit known for its strong smell.

clue.text: No orisons needed for meritoriousness presented to one honourably discharged

indicators.note: tells you the letters of the prayers are absent from the long word
the remaining letters are offered up in a new order

explanation.surface: Merit needs no prayers when an award goes to a retiree with honours.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of ORISONS (prayers) from MERITORIOUSNESS; EMERITUS is what remains, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor retired with an honorary title is one discharged from duties with honour.

clue.text: Clamour at college, sound of pride

parts.note: up means at university, as in 'up at Oxford'
a pride of lions makes a roar

explanation.surface: Noise on campus, a sound of self-esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' is a group of lions, not vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud noisy outcry is a clamour.

clue.text: Report of shot at home

parts.note: a bullet is a shot
in means at home

explanation.surface: An account of a gunshot at a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A short news statement is a report.

clue.text: Remove from power

parts.note: sounds like deposing a ruler, but means pulling a lead from a socket

explanation.surface: Depose someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulling a lead out of the mains disconnects a device from its electricity supply.

clue.text: Rt Hon mixed up in a French move to topple

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside

parts.note: une is French for a

indicators.note: mixed up means jumbled or confused, so the letters of Rt Hon do not stay in the order printed

explanation.surface: A confused British MP in a French move to overthrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Rt Hon (Right Honourable) is a title of British MPs; 'mixed up' makes THRON, put 'in' UNE.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a monarch from the throne is to topple them.

clue.text: Shylock, perhaps, firm in old city

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city in Mesopotamia
sure means firm

explanation.surface: Shylock, a solid citizen in an ancient town.
explanation.definitionFit: Shylock in The Merchant of Venice is a moneylender charging interest, an example.
